items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: The transcript mentions Joey Bishop in the context of Frank Sinatra's show and Tommy Dorsey's engagement, but the interviewee (Cliff Leeman) does not describe a personal interaction, professional collaboration, or direct relationship with Joey Bishop.

ctx.x: The office had talked Tommy Dorsey into making up -- their standing feud over the years with his brother Jimmy, and it was then that it was the Dorsey Brothers, and we opened the Paramount Theatre -- great publicity for Frank and his picture.

The engagement was a smash success -- and it was four weeks, a month -- and that was the first time, a first for Joey Bishop. Frank had heard Joey Bishop and liked his work, so that was the comedian that was on the bill, that was the first time for Joey Bishop on Broadway.

Tommy and Jimmy did a medley of all their hits over the years -- the ones that Jimmy did with his band and Tom with his band, and I think we did about 20 minutes. The rest of the show, we played for Frank Sinatra, and he put on a hell of a show, as he always does, and it was his music. So we played 40 to 50 minutes behind Frank Sinatra, and that was plenty of music to play. But we didn't feature the band that much.
